sections.name: Crude oil
sections.read: The prompt is still paid over, but the balance has turned. Supply is back above demand for the first time since the war began. What is short now is oil in tanks on land.
sections.flows_note: Gulf, Red Sea and Russian loadings are what AIS can see. The IEA puts Gulf exports at 74% of pre-war, so most of that oil sails unseen.

Supply.text: World supply reached 105.4 mb/d in October, up 5.3 mb/d since August.
Gulf exports outside Oman were 18.4 mb/d in October, still 26% below pre-war. Part of it crosses Hormuz dark.
Saudi exports through the Red Sea fell under the Houthi embargo. That is the drop in the Yanbu and Fujairah line of the chart from late July.

Demand.text: World demand falls 2.7 mb/d this year to 102.3 mb/d, then recovers 2 mb/d in 2027. The fourth quarter runs a surplus of about 1.7 mb/d, the first since the war began.

Stocks.text: Observed stocks rose 52 Mbbl in October, the first build since June. Oil on water took 86 Mbbl, so stocks on land kept falling and are the lowest since at least 2016.
Stocks are down 462 Mbbl since the war began. Governments have released 349 Mbbl of reserves, with 71 Mbbl still to come by the end of February.

Watch.text: Brent settled at 92.57 $/bbl on 20 November, down 3.4% on the week. It was the third weekly loss in a row.

Trump said on 20 November that Iran wants a deal, but not one Washington accepts. Two tankers were attacked in the strait the next day. A real reopening of Hormuz would move the oil on water into tanks.
OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November to set their 2027 output policy.

sections.name: Diesel and gasoil
sections.read: Diesel is the shortage that has not gone away. Crude came back faster than the refineries that turn it into distillate.

Supply.text: Gulf product and LPG exports run at about half of pre-war.
Russia shipped 985 kt of diesel in October and 427 kt in September, against about 2.7 Mt a month a year earlier.
Ukrainian drone strikes have cut Russian refinery runs by 45% since late October, to about 3 mb/d. They disrupted or halted 15 of the 35 large refineries.

Demand.text: European diesel costs close to 180 $/bbl, 77% above pre-war.
US retail diesel averaged 5.86 $/gal on 21 November, against 3.80 a year earlier.

Stocks.text: US distillate stocks rose 1.6 Mbbl to 104.9 Mbbl in the week to 13 November. That is still about 6 Mbbl less than a year earlier.

Watch.text: Russian diesel has been allowed into the US since the waiver of 9 October. No cargo had been delivered by 19 November.

sections.name: Gasoline
sections.read: Gasoline is the product the world has enough of. Refiners run hard for diesel and make gasoline along the way.

Supply.text: US refineries ran 16.9 mb/d of crude in the week to 13 November, at 95.7% of capacity. Every extra barrel run for diesel makes gasoline too.
ARA gasoline stocks fell by nearly 7% on the week.

Demand.text: US gasoline demand averaged 8.68 mb/d over the four weeks to 13 November, down 1.8% on the year.
The northwest European gasoline crack is back in the mid teens of $/bbl. Gulf Coast gasoline cracks fell while diesel cracks rose.
Regular gasoline averaged 3.66 $/gal at the pump on 21 November, against 3.09 a year earlier.

Stocks.text: US gasoline stocks rose 5.2 Mbbl to 215.9 Mbbl in the week to 13 November, about 8.6 Mbbl more than a year earlier.

Watch.text: The switch to summer grade lifts RBOB from April. That is the step on the curve, not a shortage.

sections.name: Natural gas and LNG
sections.read: Europe goes into winter with storage 14 points under normal and Qatar still under force majeure. The US is long gas at home, which is the whole arbitrage.
sections.flows_note: Ras Laffan is counted in tanker calls, because an LNG carrier hardly changes draught. The count includes condensate and LPG ships, and only what AIS can see.

Supply.text: QatarEnergy has kept force majeure on LNG since March and extends it month by month. Poland's Orlen cited it to end its 2009 supply contract on 10 November.
Two trains at Ras Laffan were hit in March. That takes out 12.8 Mt a year, about 17% of Qatar's capacity, for three to five years.
Only two LNG carriers crossed Hormuz in the week to 17 November, against about eight a week over the two months before.

Demand.text: Europe took 54% of US LNG exports in September, 5.91 Mt of 10.9 Mt.
Europe is on track to import 10.11 Mt of LNG in November, up from 8.99 Mt in October.

Stocks.text: EU storage was 69.8% full on 18 November, down from a peak of 75.0%. 11% of the gas injected over the summer has already been withdrawn.

Watch.text: North Field East has its first train ready in November, with production due in the first quarter of 2027.
A dozen empty carriers wait off Qatar. They would show a restart before any statement does.

sections.name: Thermal coal
sections.read: Indonesia ships a quarter less than last year and India is buying again. Coal is also the cheap fuel while gas costs what it does.
sections.flows_note: Dry bulk through coal ports is mostly coal, but not only. Rotterdam and Amsterdam also land ore.

Supply.text: Indonesia cut its 2026 output quota from 817.5 Mt to about 600 Mt, then moved it back toward 720 Mt. August exports were 36.1 Mt, down 23% on the year.
Supply.source: Reuters and Fitch via Discovery Alert, 20 Oct 2026

Supply.text: Drought on the Barito River cut the draught to 3 or 4 metres and roughly halved barge loads.
China mined 380 Mt of raw coal in October, down 5.8% on the year, and 3,830 Mt in ten months, down 3.8%.

Demand.text: India imported 15.06 Mt of thermal coal in October, its highest month since May 2025.
South Korea imported 9.59 Mt of coal of all kinds in October, a five-month low and 4.4% less than a year earlier.

Watch.text: Indonesia plans to route all exports through one state gateway from 1 January 2027, and its 2027 quota is not out yet.
Coal India produced 67.2 Mt in October, up 19%. More coal at home is what ends an Indian import run.

sections.name: Coking coal
sections.read: China lost supply at home and now buys Australian coal that used to go to India.
sections.flows_note: Gladstone also ships thermal coal, so the Queensland line is a little wider than coking coal.

Supply.text: Australia shipped 12.49 Mt in October, up 1.8% on the year, and 126.5 Mt in ten months, up 4.3%.
A mine accident in Shanxi in May cut Chinese output. The shortage is expected to last into 2027.
Strict safety inspections still hold back Chinese mines. Low-sulphur coal in Linfen was quoted at 2,230 yuan/t on 20 November, and the market expects a fourth cut in coke prices.

Demand.text: China took 18.65 Mt of Australian coking coal in ten months, up 89%.
India took 27.94 Mt, down 14.6%, and its share of Australian exports fell from 27% to 22%.

Watch.text: Queensland's wet season starts in December.
Indian mills coming back to restock would meet Chinese buying on the same coal.

sections.name: Iron ore
sections.read: Ore is piling up in Chinese ports while mills make less iron. Simandou adds tonnes from further away.
sections.flows_note: The six Chinese ports are the large northern ore terminals. They also land some coal.

Supply.text: World shipments were 170.4 Mt in October, up 0.65% on the year. Australia shipped 95.9 Mt and Brazil 40.3 Mt.
Guinea shipped more than 5 Mt in October for the first time and became the third largest exporter. More than 22 Mt have left this year as Simandou ramps up.

Demand.text: China imported 105.7 Mt in October, down 5.0% on the year, and 1,060.6 Mt in ten months, up 3.1%.
Hot metal output was 2.348 Mt a day on 18 November, 15 kt a day less than a week earlier and the lowest in five weeks.
China made 70.83 Mt of crude steel in October, down 1.6% on the year, and 795.61 Mt in ten months, down 2.8%.

Stocks.text: Stocks at 35 Chinese ports were 153.75 Mt on 20 November, up 1.63 Mt on the week. It was the fourth weekly build in a row.

Watch.text: Every Simandou tonne that replaces an Australian one triples the voyage. That is bearish for ore and supportive for Capesizes.

sections.name: Steel and scrap
sections.read: The US is short behind a 50% tariff and everyone else is long. Scrap follows Turkish mills, who buy cargo by cargo.

Supply.text: China exported 95.5 Mt of steel in ten months, down 2.3% on the year, and 9.85 Mt in October.
Supply.source: Chinese customs via GMK Center, 10 Nov 2026

Supply.text: US finished steel imports fell 14% to about 13 Mt in nine months. Their market share went from 19% to 16%.

Demand.text: US coil reached 1,445 $/st on 19 November, its highest since April 2022, and was at 1,421 the next day.
The EU coil quota is exhausted. On 19 November Turkey and the FTA pool had none left for the quarter, India about 1.5 kt and Vietnam about 3.7 kt.

Scrap.text: HMS 80:20 averaged 397 $/t CFR Turkey in October. Turkey imported 14.3 Mt in nine months, up 2.3%.
Turkish mills buy hand to mouth, with lending rates at 49% and rebar margins negative.
HMS 80:20 held at 405 $/t CFR Turkey on 19 November.

Watch.text: The EU plans to restrict scrap exports to non-OECD countries from May 2027.
The EU put anti-dumping duties of up to 27.9% on cold-rolled steel from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkey and Vietnam from 17 November.

sections.name: Copper
sections.read: There is enough copper in the world and it sits in the wrong place. Most visible stock is in the US, while China pays a record premium to import.

Supply.text: Grasberg ran at about two thirds of its normal rate in the third quarter and is not due back at full rate before late 2027.
Cochilco expects Chile's output to fall 8.4% this year to 4.94 Mt, the lowest in 23 years.

Demand.text: The Yangshan import premium reached 360 $/t on 18 November, from less than 100 in September.
The ICSG sees a refined surplus of 104 kt this year and 368 kt next. Goldman puts the market outside the US in a 950 kt deficit.

Stocks.text: LME stocks were 332,025 t on 20 November, up from 274,000 t at the end of October.
COMEX holds 730,697 t, near its record, and almost 74% of LME stock sits in US warehouses. Shanghai fell to 27,642 t, the lowest since December 2023.

Watch.text: The 15% tariff that Commerce proposed on refined copper from January 2027 still awaited a presidential decision on 19 November.
COMEX went from more than 700 $/t over the LME in August to slightly under it.
LME cash copper fell to 12,230.50 $/t on 20 November, from 13,610 a week earlier.

sections.name: Aluminium
sections.read: Gulf smelters ship through Hormuz and a good part of their metal is still missing. Premiums say the shortage is in the West.

Supply.text: War damage and the strait cut output at the affected Gulf and European smelters by an estimated 44%, from 6.15 Mt to 3.45 Mt a year.
EGA has restored 61% of its Al Taweelah smelter and expects full production in the first quarter of 2027.

Demand.text: A Reuters poll sees a deficit of about 720 kt this year and a surplus of 410 kt in 2027. Citi has 941 kt, then a surplus of 1.8 Mt.
Demand.source: Reuters poll via Discovery Alert, 16 Nov 2026

Demand.text: The Rotterdam duty-paid premium fell to 470 to 500 $/t on 13 November, from 540 to 570 three days earlier.
Japan's fourth quarter premium settled at 255 $/t, down from 395.
Demand.source: Fastmarkets and Platts via Discovery Alert, 2 Nov 2026

Stocks.text: LME stocks were 223,525 t on 20 November. Cash settled 353 $/t over three months, against about 35 at the end of October.
The squeeze is the tightest since those of 1988 and 1990. All but 50 t of the metal on LME warrant at the end of October was Russian.

Watch.text: Rotterdam premium futures fall sharply from January. The market is pricing the Gulf recovery before it has happened.
The US tariff is 50% of the metal value, so the Midwest premium moves with the LME price.

sections.name: Crude tankers
sections.read: Rates are off their October record and still an order of magnitude above normal. Ships are scarce where it is dangerous to load.

Demand.text: Seaborne crude flows were 45.7 mb/d in October, down 6.6% on the year.
Moving a barrel from the Gulf to East Asia cost 37.13 $ in freight and 12.29 $ in insurance in late October, against 3.18 and 0.06 in January. That is about 30% of the delivered price.

Supply.text: 47 empty VLCCs were heading west, down from 49. East of Suez 450 VLCCs were in ballast on 12 November against 308 laden.
The crude tanker orderbook was 14.1% of the fleet a year ago, a nine-year high, with deliveries peaking in 2027. Close to a fifth of the fleet is over 20 years old.

Rates.text: At the peak on 16 October a VLCC earned 1.37 M$ a day from the Gulf to China, and Houston to China paid 80.6 M$ a voyage.
Atlantic rates bounced back this week. An Aframax from Houston to Rotterdam was assessed 283 points higher at just over WS 596, about 180,100 $ a day.

Watch.text: A confirmed Hormuz deal would cut war premiums first and voyage lengths second.
Crude and heavy product export volumes were down 5.7% in the year to August. Rates are high on lost ship time, not on more cargo.
Five tankers were struck near Hormuz between 11 and 18 November.

sections.name: Product tankers
sections.read: Clean tankers out of the Gulf earn crude money. An MR from Rotterdam to New York earns about 27 times less, and one leaving the US Gulf sits in between.

Demand.text: Seaborne clean product exports reached 18.4 mb/d in October, about 5% below the 2025 average.
Only about 12% of the Aframax and LR2 fleet trades clean, near a record low. MRs carried 55% of clean cargo in October, against 48% in 2025.

Supply.text: 116 MRs and 73 LR2s were delivered this year. Another 163 MRs and 82 LR2s are due by the end of 2027, 8% and 11% of their fleets.

Rates.text: An LR2 from the Gulf to Japan earned 308,200 $ a day on 20 November. An MR earned 23,700 from the US Gulf to Europe and 11,300 from Rotterdam to New York, after the Atlantic MR basket fell from 60,600 to 37,000 in a week.

Watch.text: Russian diesel is allowed back into the Atlantic since the US waiver of 9 October, long-haul work for MRs out of the Baltic. No cargo had been delivered to the US by 19 November.

sections.name: LNG carriers
sections.read: There are too many LNG ships. Rates collapsed with the gas market at its tightest since 2022, because the gas sails short voyages to Europe.

Demand.text: Europe took 54% of US LNG in September, so ships turn round quickly and come back to the prompt market.

Supply.text: 55 carriers were delivered in the first seven months of 2026. Close to 100 are due this year and about 95 in 2027.
The orderbook is about 285 ships, some 37% of the fleet.
Supply.source: FLEX LNG via Ship Universe, 7 Oct 2026

Rates.text: Spot rates were 20,500 $ a day in the Atlantic and 52,000 in the Pacific on 19 November. They peaked at 287,500 and 225,750 in early March.

Watch.text: A Qatari restart would pull ships east and lengthen voyages. Until then every new delivery adds to the surplus.

sections.name: Dry bulk carriers
sections.read: Capesizes earn about 40,000 $ a day on Pacific ore and longer hauls. From next year the fleet grows faster than the cargo.

Demand.text: With the strait closed, BIMCO sees ship demand growing 0.5 to 2.5% in 2027 and coal shipments falling.
Guinean ore sails 88% further than the average iron ore cargo. Iron ore tonne-miles rose 2% in ten months on flat volumes.

Supply.text: Supply grows 3 to 4% in 2027 as deliveries pick up, Capesizes above all.
Dry bulk recycling fell 36% to 3 M dwt in ten months, the lowest in 18 years. Deliveries are expected to grow 19% in 2027.

Rates.text: The Baltic Dry Index closed at 2,898 on 20 November, down 2.8% on the week. The Capesize index lost 4.6%.
Rates.source: Baltic Exchange via Baird Maritime, 20 Nov 2026

Rates.text: Ultramaxes across the Atlantic still pay high 30,000s $ a day for November, down from 39,000 to 42,000 last week. December looks more balanced.

Watch.text: Bulk carriers returning to the Panama Canal would shorten voyages.
